ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Preventive Visit — Wilma Mankiller

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Periodic preventive visit; no new complaints. [S]

Ms. Mankiller, a 34-year-old woman with generalized myasthenia gravis, returns for her periodic preventive visit eleven weeks after robotic thymectomy. She completed the health risk assessment beforehand. Her eyelids no longer droop and double vision has not returned; she tires a little by late afternoon. She takes pyridostigmine 60 mg four times daily, prednisone (now 30 mg each morning and tapering), azathioprine 150 mg daily, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole three times a week, calcium and vitamin D. She sleeps less well on prednisone and has gained about 3 kg since the spring. She has had no breathlessness, swallowing trouble or infections. She is back at work most days and walks with a cane only on rough ground. She asks which vaccines and screening she needs while on these medicines. [S]

Follow-up: Seven-month review in seven weeks with neuromuscular neurology input, blood count, liver and kidney tests, hemoglobin A1c and urine albumin. Influenza and COVID-19 vaccines then. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-12: seven-month review: minimal manifestation status, prednisone and pyridostigmine reduction, azathioprine safety, kidney screening, and plans for the year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with her consent. She named a health care agent, and a health care proxy form was completed; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. She said that what matters most to her is to keep working for her community, to be told plainly what is happening, and to make her own decisions, with her own Cherokee medicine respected. She chose not to record specific treatment preferences today, and knows that the plan can be updated at any visit. [S]
